g.text: Figure 9 Structured Class Diagram — A1 Orchestrator
(internal parts, ports and connectors; A1 is the LangGraph StateGraph itself, 18.2)
Tier 5 consumers of the provided interfaces
+ GATE-R, PLN-18, ACC-10, GEN-14 via interrupt()
kind x decision, gate x disposition
deterministic, no LLM; inputs are only
the procedure pack, the dependency DAG
A checkpoint is not the audit trail (18.5)
A1 never calls the LLM (4.1): every part is
deterministic Python. A1 writes only phase,
computed here and is not editable (M-12).
mergePatch reducer (18.3.1): one writer per field;
a new id is appended; the same id is overwritten by
the higher version; equal versions conflict and go
to a human. Agents never call each other, so fan-in
A1 publishes tasks and ranks none of them: A6 instances and
the A5 event stream draft ReviewTasks, A1 merges the patch,
writes the business results, publishes the drafts and sets
status to decided once a ReviewRecord passes DecisionSubmit.
The one task A1 creates itself: kind failed, when a patch is
rejected twice (8.6). An empty queue does not hold the next layer.
decisionPort: A1 realises StateQuery and DecisionSubmit
ReviewRecord or GateDecision and checks targetVersion,
gate state and the task kind x decision matrix before
writing (18.5, UC-04). The panel and the fallback forms
at fan_in and after every decision:
«part» internal part of the structured class;
owned by A1, not shared with any other component
port / portin / portout named interaction point on the
A1 boundary; the thin line inside A1 is a delegation
connector from the port to the owning part
( ) provided interface, offered at a port
--( required interface, consumed at a port
solid arrow between parts connector, labelled with
dashed arrow to TrailWriter logging connector
